I am still doing the usual wheat-maize rotation on my 6.5 mu. Land is not much, so I cannot take big risks. What keeps the family steady is better than chasing something fancy. I have farmed this way many years. Wheat goes in after the autumn rains, around early October, and maize follows right after wheat harvest in June. The time between the two crops is very tight, so after cutting wheat I do only simple field cleaning and quick tillage, then plant maize fast. If I delay, the maize loses days and yield.

For seed, I buy what people around here commonly use from the local dealer. I do not save on seed too much, because if emergence is poor, that loss is bigger than the extra seed money. Fertilizer, I use in the same rough way as before. I would rather not let the crop look weak. For wheat, I put most of the fertilizer before sowing, then add some urea at jointing if the leaves are not dark enough. Wheat needs more water here, so I plan a few well irrigations if rain is not enough. For maize, I keep it simpler: base fertilizer when planting, then one topdress around the big growing stage. If summer rain is decent, maybe I irrigate once, maybe not. Pesticide I only use when I see a real problem, mostly herbicide first, then insecticide if needed. Family labor is enough for most work, but if the wheat harvest and maize planting are too rushed, I may pay for a little machine help or hired labor. I am not trying to calculate exact best numbers. I just want both crops to grow steadily, not spend too much cash at once, and make sure the land does not sit empty.
